newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI welcomes proposed change in ownership.
newsitem.headline: JCI welcomes proposed change in ownership.

text.p: JCI Ltd said on Tuesday it welcomed the proposed sale to black business of all or part of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd's stake in the company.

"There will be significant benefits for our current operations in South African and to our expansion plans, especially in Africa, of having controlling black shareholders," the South African mining house said in an announcement accompanying its year end results.

"Their involvement has the potential to unlock value to all by boosting the initiatives already underway across the group, especially our gold operations, to secure more productive relationships between labour and management and to change our culture generally."
JCI said it was keen to facilitate a speedy resolution to the proposed change in shareholding.
At the same time, JCI was committed to an ongoing review of its strategy and aimed to create a new entrepreneurial culture within the group, it said.

It was, together with Anglo, in discussion with various prospective investors to ensure that owners and management were up to speed about the future of the company when the change of ownership took place.

The future of JCI has moved into the spotlight following last month's landmark deal under which Anglo and De Beers will sell the bulk of their stake in sister company Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd to black investors.

Anglo finance director Michael King said last week that five black-led groups had separately expressed interest in JCI: New Africa Investments Ltd, Real Africa Investments Ltd, African Renaissance, Thebe Investments and Capital Alliance.
